objective: RANK 1 IS A RED TEAM PASS OVER BATCH-007, BATCH-008 AND BATCH-009 TOGETHER, and it exists because none of the three has ever had one and their results now compose into a single narrative nobody has attacked as a whole. BATCH-007 proved Proposition 1 (W = 4 - |A| at r <= 4, smask in 1..14): the r <= 4 statistic is a CERTAINTY by theorem, not a measurement. BATCH-008 excluded byte-locality for the r=5 excess (k=1,2,3 all consistent with the analytic null; only the full 4-byte word shows excess) and found it is not AES-S-box-specific (BATCH-006's own 27 random-S-box arms put AES at the 41st percentile of its own null distribution). BATCH-009 excluded probe-geometry-plus-counting as an explanation: the excess does NOT survive substituting the cipher with a lazily-sampled ideal permutation (14 vs 1 at matched exposure, sharpening to 18.7x [6.74, 59.27] at 8x exposure on the null arm alone). Three negative results, each independently checked by exactly one validator and never by an adversary, now jointly imply something has NOT been said out loud in this campaign: whatever produces the r=5 excess is neither a counting artifact, nor S-box-specific, nor byte-local, nor a property of a structureless permutation. The red team's job is to find where that chain is weaker than it looks, not to restate it.

tasks.title: RED TEAM: attack BATCH-007, BATCH-008 and BATCH-009 as a composed narrative

handoff.objective: Attack the composed BATCH-007/008/009 narrative -- that the r=5 excess is a real phenomenon, neither a counting artifact, nor S-box-specific, nor byte-local, nor a probe-geometry artifact -- for the weakest link, not to restate that the three batches individually pass.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether the three negative results, taken together, actually narrow what could explain the r=5 excess, or whether a shared blind spot across all three (same instrument lineage, same key, same probe geometry, same model resolving every party) undermines the composition.
inputs: The three governing decisions DEC-20260803-147e9d, DEC-20260803-f6f113, DEC-20260805-9a1c47
deliverables: AN EXPLICIT RULING ON THE COMPOSED CLAIM. State plainly whether 'not byte-local, not S-box-specific, not a probe-geometry artifact, not a counting artifact at r<=4' actually composes into a narrower target for what DOES explain the excess, or whether the four exclusions are not as independent as they look -- e.g. because BATCH-008's and BATCH-009's null objects share more structure with each other and with the live arm than their names suggest.
A NAMED WEAKEST LINK. Of the three batches, identify which result is least robust to an adversarial reading, and why -- not which is wrong, but which would break first under further scrutiny.

AN ATTACK ON THE SHARED-INSTRUMENT-LINEAGE RISK. yoyo_sbox_v2 through v4 form one lineage of additions-only diffs from a common ancestor. If a bug were present in the ORIGINAL v2 base and never removed, every equivalence proof in this campaign (each of which checks a NEW version against the PRIOR version, never against an independent reimplementation of the whole probe from the specification) would pass while carrying the same bug forward. Rule on whether this risk is live and, if so, what the cheapest control against it would be.

A CHECK ON THE SEED/KEY REUSE ACROSS BATCH-008 AND BATCH-009. Both used seed 531001, armid 1, amask 1, smask 1 -- the SAME derived key -- to enable direct bit-exact comparison across batches. State plainly whether that shared key introduces any risk that the r=5 excess is a property of THIS ONE KEY rather than a property of the round structure in general, and whether any arm in this campaign has ever tested a second key at r=5 under the SAME probe geometry.

AN ABSENCE-CLAIM SEARCH, IF ANY IS MADE. If this report claims anything was never tested, run the search per CORR-20260803-8fa302's rule and record it in this artifact -- the glob or grep executed, the file count, the date -- in the SAME document as the claim.

A RULING ON WHETHER FURTHER PURSUIT IS WARRANTED, per docs/inventor-protocol.md's closure standard. Not a recommendation to pause or continue in the abstract -- a ruling with a stated evidence basis, budget, test boundary, remaining uncertainty and a concrete next construction or revisit condition, per AGENTS.md rule 9 on premature closure being symmetric with overclaiming.
constraints: AUDIT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. This campaign has understated its own evidence at least as often as it has overstated it in the last three days; do not assume the failure mode you are looking for is overclaiming.

DO NOT RE-RUN THE MEASUREMENTS. This is a review of reasoning, composition and instrument lineage, not a fourth measurement batch. If you find a control that MUST be run to settle a specific doubt, name it as a ranked next action rather than running it yourself.
TOY TIER. Nothing about full-round or deployed AES; no comparison to published cryptanalysis in either direction.

INFERENCE BLOCK: policy, requested_policy, ACTUAL resolved model, fallback_used, model_verified (false, no adapter probe exists), standing basis 0137a051eb5828789eb267fa83c8278086578d4c. State session-but-NOT-model independence explicitly: every party in this campaign resolves to one model, and this report supplies no closure-quorum independence.
EVERY STRUCTURED ARTIFACT MUST PARSE. Parse the WHOLE file before finishing, not the last-edited region, and say inside the artifact that you did.
